name: Tree, TREE!!!
description: Roots change, but the tree stands strong — so should your logic. Behruzbek received a tree $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ with $$$n$$$ nodes. For a chosen root $$$^{\text{†}}$$$ $$$r$$$, Behruzbek wants to find cuteness of the tree. Consider every set of $$$k$$$ distinct nodes of the tree. For each such set, compute its lowest common ancestor ( LCA ) in the tree when it is rooted at $$$r$$$. Let $$$S_r$$$ be the set of all distinct nodes obtained this way; then cuteness of the tree is $$$|S_r|$$$, where $$$|S|$$$ means the number of distinct elements. After discovering the cuteness of trees, Behruzbek became interested in finding the kawaiiness of the tree! Kawaiiness is defined as: $$$$$$ \sum_{r = 1}^{n} |S_r| = |S_1| + |S_2| + \dots + |S_n| $$$$$$ Unfortunately, Behruzbek is feeling sleepy now. Please help Behruzbek by finding the kawaiiness of the tree! $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. $$$^{\text{†}}$$$A rooted tree is a tree where one vertex is special and called the root.
input_specification: The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^{4}$$$). The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \leq k \leq n \leq 2\cdot 10^{5}$$$) — the number of vertices in the tree and the number of distinct integers to be chosen. The following $$$n-1$$$ lines of each test case describe the tree. Each of the lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \leq u,v \leq n$$$, $$$u \ne v$$$) that indicate an edge between vertex $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that these edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2\cdot 10^{5}$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output one integer — the value of $$$\sum\limits_{r=1}^n |S_r|$$$.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2167F — Tree, TREE!!! [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
